Motivation comes and goes; systems stay. Today you don\'t need to feel like it, you need a 2-minute step. Pick the smallest action from your goal for the month and do it now. Then check it off in Today: seeing your progress lights the fire again.

Before you give up, open the Anti-quitting bonus: most of the time you don\'t need to leave the mountain, just change the route. Ask yourself: does this goal still bring me closer to my summit? If the answer is yes, make the step smaller, not the goal.

Getting lost in the fog is part of the journey. Open the Emergency Kit and choose the protocol that describes how you feel. Then come back to your summit in one sentence and decide only the next step.

Your Personal Summit isn\'t a geographic point or a simple goal. It\'s a state where all your dimensions converge: your willpower, your mastery, your voice, your ability to create value, your evolution and your connection with the transcendent. SuRoute helps you get there step by step: from your 5-year purpose to what you do today.

A step isn\'t ticked: it\'s earned with work days, different days you moved it forward. Every 4 stages the difficulty adjusts like Bitcoin: go too fast and a new step asks for more days; slow down and it asks for fewer so you come back. That\'s how you reach the summit on December 31.

If you are reading this, you have already taken the hardest step: you decided to climb.
SuRoute is not a to-do list. It is a map to find your summit —what gives your life meaning— and a compass so you don\'t lose it when the fog rolls in.
Here we don\'t race: we ascend. One step each day, one work day at a time, with your will, your mastery, your voice, your value, your growth and the mark you will leave on others.
There will be falls. They are part of the path, not its end. And you will not climb alone: a whole rope team walks with you.
Keep this letter. The day you reach the top, read it again.

The sky right now: the sun at %1$d°, the moon %2$d%% lit.
Earth moves between the Sun and the Moon and covers it with its shadow: the Moon turns copper. You can watch it with the naked eye, no filter needed.
Earth\'s shadow takes a bite out of the Moon. You can watch it with the naked eye, no filter needed.
The Moon passes through Earth\'s faint outer shadow and dims only slightly. It is subtle: look calmly and compare it with other nights.
The Moon passes in front of the Sun and, from Colombia, covers %1$d%% of it. Never look at it directly: use certified eclipse glasses (ISO 12312-2) or project it through a pinhole in cardboard.
Earth crosses the dust a comet left behind: each streak is a grain burning up as it enters the air. Find a dark place and look toward %1$s after midnight.
%1$s and %2$s appear almost together, %3$s° apart (less than a finger at arm\'s length). It is an apparent alignment: in reality they are millions of kilometres apart.
The full Moon coincides with its closest approach to Earth (%1$s km): it looks a little bigger and brighter.
The Sun crosses the celestial equator: today day and night last almost the same everywhere on Earth. In Colombia, at midday, the Sun passes almost straight overhead.
The Sun reaches its northernmost point of the year. In Colombia, at midday, your shadow points south.
The Sun reaches its southernmost point of the year. In Colombia, at midday, your shadow points north.

The 1·9·81 Compass is inspired by the Mandala Chart that Yasuo Matsumura created in Japan in 1979 (Matsumura, 2007). He brought the 3×3 structure of the Buddhist mandala to life and work planning: a goal at the center and eight areas around it (health, work, finances, family, society, character, learning and leisure), to live in balance (Mandala Chart Kyōkai, n.d.). Hiroaki Imaizumi turned it into Mandal-Art to generate ideas (Imaizumi, 1988) and Takashi Harada into the Open Window 64 sheet to reach goals, the one Shohei Ohtani used (Harada & Shibayama, 2017).
The Ruta a la Cima Method turns it into a mountain compass: one summit, 8 camps and 64 steps earned with workdays, measured with the Cima 9×52 Method and with one evidence photo per step.
